title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM-Generated NetOps Artifacts: a Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We study whether adding sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator increases detection of misconfigurations in LLM-generated network configuration artifacts. Using a preregistered paired-binary design (Npairs=720), a single shared-generation per task (gpt-5-mini) was evaluated under (A) baseline: deterministic validator-only and (B) guarded: validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation. Primary result: baseline detected 719/720 (99.8611%), guarded detected 720/720 (100.00%); paired difference = 0.0013889, exact McNemar two-sided p=1.0, 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.0041667]. Conclusion: for the synthetic intent→config tasks and validator used, sandboxed emulation yielded a negligible aggregate detection gain. The study is fully preregistered and executed autonomously; limitations (synthetic tasks, possible ceiling effects, single model/validator family) constrain generalization.

sections.introduction: Generative models are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into executable network configuration. Prior surveys and system papers emphasize that operational reliability depends on the surrounding machinery—validators, verifiers, emulators, and guarded workflows—rather than the model alone [1–3]. However, quantitative evidence of how much additional coverage sandboxed execution adds to a strong deterministic validator is limited. We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment to answer: For synthetic intent→configuration tasks, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) deterministic validator-only and (B) deterministic validator plus automated sandboxed emulation? Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired-binary experimental design and execution manifest; (2) an empirical result on Npairs=720 produced and analyzed under the registered pipeline; (3) a failure-mode and external-validity discussion grounded in the archived artifacts.
sections.related_work: Work on LLMs for NetOps/AIOps stresses the role of surrounding tooling and contracts (e.g., retrieval, validators, rollback) for operational safety [1,2]. Generate–validate–repair patterns are established in program verification and applied NetOps prototypes [2,4]. Recent empirical analyses show LLMs can hallucinate or err but may correct known-located mistakes if given error-localization signals [5]. There is an open call in the literature for workflow-centred benchmarks combining generation, validator checks, sandboxed execution, and rollback-aware metrics [1,3]. Our study operationalizes a narrowly scoped instance of that proposal and reports a confirmatory, artifact-grounded outcome.
sections.methodology: Preregistration: The full machine-readable preregistration (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) specified the research question, paired design, sampling plan, estimands, multiplicity, contamination controls, and analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). Key design elements: shared_initial_candidate semantics (single generation shared between paired conditions), paired N=720 confirmatory tasks, a minimum effect-of-interest of 0.20 for planning, and conservative missingness rules. Scope: synthetic LLM-generated intent→configuration tasks (intent_configuration_repair_v1 task family) produced deterministically by the registered task generator; model: gpt-5-mini via provider openai_responses; validation: deterministic_netops_validator_v5; guarded pipeline added automated sandboxed emulation after the validator per the preregistered guarded definition. Execution contract: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter; maximum_model_calls=1440; actual model_calls_used=721. All prompts, responses, validator traces, and manifests were archived; preregistration SHA-256 and initial master-prompt reference are recorded in the manifest.
sections.results: Primary confirmatory analysis (complete paired set, Npairs=720) used the preregistered paired-binary executor. Observed counts: n11=719 (detected by both), n10=1 (detected by guarded only), n01=0 (baseline-only), n00=0 (neither). Marginal rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111, guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p=1.0. Paired bootstrap (10000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% CI = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. No confirmatory secondary strata were preregistered for release; the archived artifacts include task-level traces, validator outputs, and the contingency table.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. The guarded pipeline produced one additional detection in 720 paired tasks (0.14 percentage points). This null-to-negligible effect size is robust in the archived analysis but must be interpreted in context. Possible causes: (1) ceiling effect — the deterministic validator_v5 covered the misconfiguration classes and task templates used, leaving little room for emulation to add detections; (2) synthetic tasks were constructed to be semantically explicit and parser-valid, increasing validator effectiveness; (3) shared_initial_candidate generation semantics ensured identical initial model outputs for baseline and guarded conditions, constraining sources of discordance to emulation-only observations or repair calls (the execution manifest recorded one repair stage use). Operational implication: when a high-coverage deterministic validator is available and task templates are similar to those studied, the marginal detection benefit of an added sandboxed emulation step can be very small. This does not imply sandboxing is unnecessary in general; for production heterogeneity, adversarial inputs, or validators with known coverage gaps, guarded pipelines may add meaningful protection.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing validator-only versus validator+sandboxed-emulation (guarded) pipelines on synthetic LLM-generated NetOps tasks. Aggregated across 720 paired tasks, the guarded pipeline increased detections by a trivial absolute amount (0.001389) with a two-sided p=1.0 and 95% CI [0.0, 0.0041667]. The result highlights a potential ceiling effect when high-fidelity validators already capture common misconfiguration classes in synthetic tasks. Future work should evaluate (a) broader and adversarial task banks, (b) multiple models and validator families, and (c) deployment-scale cross-vendor CLI diversity to measure where guarded pipelines materially improve operational safety.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator — reduces ecological diversity and may produce ceiling effects for strong validators.
Single model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation — limits external generalizability across model sizes and validator families.

Shared_initial_candidate design: one initial generation was shared across paired conditions, so the only allowed source of difference was downstream guarded-stage detection or repair; this choice was explicit in the preregistration but constrains the scope of discordance.
Emulation fidelity vs production networks: sandboxed execution in the study was limited to the emulation harness in the archive; real-world vendor/OS nuances and scale effects may change outcomes.
The confirmatory result is a null-to-very-small aggregate effect on this task bank; it should not be generalized to assert that sandboxed emulation never adds value in other NetOps settings.
